images.title: Fold six squares into a cube
images.purpose: Shows the core move of the net folder tool: a net of six squares folding into a cube, with opposite faces in matching colours.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Before and after in one row: the flat net on the left, a thick grey arrow, the folded cube on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: a net of 6 equal squares: a horizontal row of 4 squares (numbered left to right 1 to 4, numbers not drawn), one square above square 3 and one square below square 3; thin dark outlines and 5 thin dashed grey fold lines. Colours: squares 1 and 3 teal #0072B2, squares 2 and 4 amber #E69F00, the square above and the square below green #009E73. Under the net: '6 squares'. Centre: a thick grey arrow pointing right with 'Fold' above it. Right: a cube drawn flat in a simple corner view showing 3 faces: front face teal (square 3), top face green (the square above 3), right face amber (square 4). Under the cube: 'cube'. Nothing else.

images.takeaway: Six joined squares fold into a cube, and squares of the same colour become opposite faces.
images.description: Shows the core move of the net folder tool: a net of six squares folding into a cube, with opposite faces in matching colours.
images.context: Concept T7.C4; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Row of 4 with one above and one below the same square is a net (one of the 11). Opposite pairs: 1 and 3, 2 and 4, above and below.

image_decisions.why: The practice tool is about folding nets; the simplest fold, flat to cube, is its core manipulation.
